The strataHeaven at the top, the mortal plain at the base. Every figure holds a tier and a house — and tiers are not exclusive: a person can hold several chairs at once, each argued from its own record.
The linesDotted lines are migrations and relationships between people — and every line is labeled with what the relationship is. Unlabeled, unsourced lines don’t ship.
The entriesTap any name to open its full entry: portrait, the chairs it holds and why, its house, the record, its own verified words, every labeled line that touches it — and its song, written or not yet written.
Find a nameSearch below the throne: a person, a house, or a model — the wall lights its matches and counts them. Clear the search and the full chart returns.
The web & the lineBelow the houses, the same labeled lines are drawn as one web — trace any figure’s connections, then tap through to its entry. And the court assembles: every dated event in the records, on one chronological line, newest first.

    PASS 2 RECONCILIATION — ROSTER vs. CHART

    Every roster figure is on this chart — drawn once at their home stratum, with a dashed ghost chip wherever a second chair is held — except two names, and they are absent for two different reasons, which the chart keeps separate so they cannot be counted as one contradiction:

    NOT CAST — held out by the owner’s Rim lock: Donald Trump (roster, Villains (or Monsters) #2). He is not missing; he is excluded, by standing decision. The owner’s lock holds the Rim to the Race alone, and the graphic spec flags the political layer as not cast at launch; his Sept 14, 2026 “HOAX” post stays in the roster file, not on the wall.

    NOT YET CHAIRED — the scan’s open agenda item: Ilya Sutskever. He is not excluded; he is pending. The scan held him and the roster carries him as its open agenda item — no chair until his claim resolves. Pass 5 built his full entry at full size directly below this reconciliation — record, house line, and words — still seatless, awaiting the owner’s call. Two absences, two different doors: one locked by the owner, one waiting on the record.

    Every name on this chart is in the sources of record. The names that come from the graphic spec and anthem briefs rather than the roster’s tier tables: Sundar Pichai and Greg Brockman (spec §5.2 register — signatories of the Sept 29 Accord, which is not the pacing proposal), Gary Marcus (spec §5.5, the Grove’s amplifier-oracle), Danielle Zhang and Curt Tigges (spec §5.4 Rising cast, from the Cammarata brief’s reaction layer), Chris Painter (spec §5.4 register), and Steven Adler (spec §5.3 register). The spec’s margin registers — the Oct 13 letter’s drafters, Toby Walsh, and the 497 signers as a collective — are credited in the files and not drawn as strata in this pass. No unexplained differences remain.

    Corrections standardized in this pass: Fukushima’s neocognitron is dated 1980 everywhere (Biological Cybernetics, April 1980; the spec’s 1979 epithet was the error). Hassabis’s title is carried in its flagged split form everywhere it appears — Chair of Google DeepMind + Chief Scientist of Alphabet, day-to-day Kavukcuoglu, as of Oct 17, 2026. Meta’s flagship is carried per the spec’s handling, dated Oct 20, 2026: Muse Wonder the current flagship line (announced Oct 12, 2026), Muse Spark continuing beneath it, Llama the open line the public knows.

    NOT YET CHAIRED — A FIRST-CLASS ENTRY AWAITING ITS CHAIR

    ILYA SUTSKEVER

    the founder in the age of research

    The record. Co-author of AlexNet (2012, with Alex Krizhevsky and Geoffrey Hinton) — the paper that restarted the field — and of the sequence-to-sequence work that followed it. A doctoral student of Hinton’s at Toronto. Then the central technical figure of the lab era: co-founder of OpenAI and its chief scientist, the researcher most responsible for the programme that produced the GPT line. In November 2023 he voted, as a board member, to remove Sam Altman; days later he signed the letter calling for Altman’s return and said so in public. In May 2024 he departed OpenAI, and on June 19, 2024 he co-founded Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI) with Daniel Gross and Daniel Levy — a lab with, in its own founding words, “one goal and one product: a safe superintelligence.” He became SSI’s CEO in July 2025. His current register, in his own words: scaling alone will not finish the job — “it’s back to the age of research again, just with big computers.”

    Why no chair. His claim splits three ways at once — founder of the deep-learning era (a Godfather’s record), owner of a frontier lab (a Power’s seat), builder of a new venture in the age of research (a Rising claim) — and the roster holds him as its open agenda item for exactly that reason. The scan made no final call, and this chart does not invent one. He is not a footnote and he is not seated by stealth: this entry is his place on the wall until the call is made. Seating him is the owner’s decision alone.

    House line. OpenAI (co-founder & chief scientist) → departed, May 2024 → SSI (co-founder; CEO since July 2025). His labeled lines stand in the Heavy Lines register below; his full entry opens from the button.

    PASS 3 — THE WEB, DEEPENED

    The lines more than doubled where it counts. Pass 3 drew the web out of the sources of record: descent lines (Barto → Sutton, Poggio → Hassabis), co-invention and co-authorship (Hinton–Sejnowski; Schmidhuber–Hochreiter’s LSTM), the 2018 Turing co-laureates’ three-way bond across the Godfathers’ flank, corroboration and testimony (Hubinger → Coxon; Turner and Kokotajlo beside him, Oct 5), the pacing weekend’s endorsements and its one dissent, the argument inside Goodfire (Gorton against Cammarata; Tigges beside him), and founder lines down to the houses (Bengio → Mila, Barnes → METR, Hobbhahn → Apollo). Every line is labeled and sourced in the files of record; nothing unsourced was drawn. One endpoint is new to the wall: Koray Kavukcuoglu stands in the Powers’ register so the succeeded (day-to-day) line has both its people on the chart — sourced from the graphic spec’s house fields (the DeepMind succession, Aug 2026), not a roster chair. Fei-Fei Li’s founder line to World Labs stands in the register above: World Labs holds no house card on the wall yet, so that line is carried in text, not drawn — the grammar only draws what the wall holds.

    Readability: drawn labels are placed by a collision pass — each one is tried against every chip, card and heading on the wall and set in the clearest gap, on its own ground. On the phone, the register is the lines’ home — browsable by name, not one long dump.

    PASS 4 — POLISH & THE POSTER

    The final pass changed no casting. The wall was finished as a poster — framed, its strata headed large enough to read across a room, the cast stamp set prominent at the top — and every entry drawer was proofread for consistency: the same fields, in the same order, for every figure. The reconciliation above was reworded so its two absences read as what they are: one name not cast, one name not yet chaired. What the owner left open stays open: the apex seat is still empty, the Rim still holds only the Race, the two tier names are still pending his pick, and Sam Altman still sits as a Power and OpenAI’s leader — one chair, in the light.

    PASS 5 — THE COURT COMPLETED & THE OPEN CHAIR

    The Celestial Court stands complete. Four owed courts were verified from primary sources and drawn: MiniMax (the company’s own site; Yan Junjie; the M2.5 / M3 line; Hailuo), StepFun (the company’s own site, which headlines Step 5 Preview as its frontier model; Jiang Daxin, founder & CEO), Baichuan (Wang Xiaochuan, founder & CEO; Baichuan 4 and the medical Baichuan-M line, from the company’s launch record and its own published papers), and 01.AI (Kai-Fu Lee, founder & CEO; Yi-Lightning, named the flagship in the company’s own technical report). No court was drawn on a guess; every field carries the chart’s stamp, as of Oct 17, 2026.

    The open chair got its entry. Ilya Sutskever’s full entry now stands above, under NOT YET CHAIRED — record, house line, and his own words, at full size. He holds no tier chair: the three-way split in his claim is the roster’s open agenda item, and seating is the owner’s call alone. Nothing else moved: the apex is still empty, the Rim still holds only the Race, no named person is cast as a Villain (or Monster), the two pending tier names are still pending, and Sam Altman still sits as a Power and OpenAI’s leader only.

    PASS 6 — EVERY FIGURE, FULL ENTRY; PORTRAITS; SEARCH

    The open chair’s standard became everyone’s. The full-entry pattern Sutskever’s entry set in Pass 5 — portrait, chairs with their reasons, house, the record, the figure’s own sourced words where the sources carry them, every labeled line, and a song slot — now stands behind every one of the chart’s 56 entries. The song slot is universal: it names the anthem brief or story song where one exists (the Coxon, Cammarata, LeCun and Hinton anthems; the Pace ensemble; “Sign the Letter” and its named signers and its dissenter) and reads Song: not yet written where none does — the backlog is printed, not hidden.

    The faces arrived. Fifty-five plates from the show’s portrait catalog are wired in — 38 graded likeness in the catalog’s review, 14 graded evocation, and 3 veiled. Likenesses present as portraits; evocations carry the caption stylized evocation in their entries and are never passed off as the person’s face. Figures whose plates are still being painted wear a monogram, and the wiring is a lookup — when the next batch lands, the plates swap in without touching a line of the chart. And the symmetry rule holds everywhere: one uniform size and crop for every portrait on the wall — no figure’s head is larger than another’s, because on this chart size is meaning. The Celestial Court’s eleven leaders stand among them — where a leader’s face is not publicly verified, the plate is veiled in porcelain, the chart’s mark that the seat is carried by record, not by likeness.

    The wall can be searched. The finder above the chart takes a person, a house, or a model and lights the matches where they stand — nothing moves, so the dotted lines stay true, and the Heavy Lines register keeps its own browse-by-name filter alongside. Nothing else moved: the apex is still empty, the Rim still holds only the Race, no named person is cast as a Villain (or Monster), the two pending tier names are still pending, Sam Altman still sits as a Power and OpenAI’s leader only, and Ilya Sutskever is still not yet chaired.

    PASS 8 — THE WEB & THE TIMELINE

    The chart’s two reading views. The web draws every person-to-person line in the registers as one graph — twenty labeled lines between twenty-five figures — built at load from the same line data the wall draws, plus the two labeled lines the wall carries in text only (Hinton–LeCun, the third side of the Turing triangle; Sutskever–Hinton, the doctoral line). No line was drawn that the records do not label and source; figures with no sourced line to another figure stand unlinked in their tier column, and the web says so. The timeline assembles the court from the records’ own dates — papers, foundings, launches, departures, testimony, the letters — each event linked to its people’s entries and its houses’ cards, and the “this week on the wall” strip under the masthead is fed by the same dated log. Nothing else moved: the apex is still empty, the Rim still holds only the Race, and Ilya Sutskever is still not yet chaired — he stands in the web under his own heading, the Open Chair, wired to the one line the record gives him.

    Cast by documented record only; allegations are labeled allegations, and membership is revisable — the record changes, the casting changes. Two tier names remain the owner’s either/or picks: Villains (or Monsters) and Harbingers (or Farseers / Soothsayers). The portraits are stylized plates from the show’s catalog, graded figure by figure: likenesses are presented as portraits, plates graded evocation are captioned as stylized evocations in their entries — an atmospheric plate, never an identifying likeness — and plates graded veiled wear the porcelain mask: the leader’s seat is a matter of public record, but no verified face exists to paint, so none is invented. Every portrait displays at one uniform size and crop.
